# A test reads a component var named `length`, and a node prop whose value
# reads it. `length` is a member of a list, a map and a string; on anything
# else it is the name the program gave, and the Go emitter wrote `len(c)` for
# a read of it off the instance.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

component box node {
    var length = 3
    text #out(value="{length}")
}

func testReadsLength(t Test, c box) {
    t.assert(c.length == 3)
    t.assert(c.out.value == "3")
}

window {
    box
}
